summary: Decision 8 pass (batch rs-cbi-3): rules each document states that were already recorded from other sources, now recorded from this document too.

program_terms.applies_to: minimum holding period for the pre-approved real estate investment
program_terms.quote: invest a minimum of US$270,000 in pre-approved real estate projects with a five-year minimum holding period
program_terms.notes: Number written in words ('five-year'). The Box does not state from when this applies. No other source in the data records this Grenada rule yet.

program_terms.applies_to: share of all National Transformation Fund receipts set aside into a Contingency or Rainy-Day Fund
program_terms.quote: The actual set aside of 10 percent of all National Transformation Fund receipts into a Contingency or Rainy-Day Fund to support recovery in the event of a major economic shock.
program_terms.notes: Budget Statement, March 2025. No start date given here (the April 2023 event from another source covers the change). No term row for this rule exists from other sources; it is recorded as events.

program_terms.applies_to: share of National Transformation Fund receipts set aside into the Contingency Fund before the government reduced it to 10 percent
program_terms.quote: our decision to reduce the percentage of the set aside from 40 per cent to 10 per cent
program_terms.notes: Earlier rule, described in passing; the Statement gives no dates for when the 40 percent applied or when it was reduced.

program_terms.applies_to: total minimum value of a tourism-accommodation unit in an approved project bought by two or more individuals
program_terms.location: p. A72, Schedule I, Sub Grouping (B)
program_terms.quote: (c) valued at a total minimum of USD $440,000.00,
program_terms.notes: Regulation 1(2): in force on 1 July 2024. S.R.O. 15 of 2024 (same commencement) states US$540,000 instead (recorded only within row t-81658909f7). SRO 12 was replaced by SRO 15 before commencement; recorded for completeness.

program_terms.applies_to: minimum equity of the total proposed construction cost invested into the approved project before an application for a shared unit is submitted to the Committee
program_terms.location: p. A72, Schedule I, Sub Grouping (B)
program_terms.quote: where a minimum equity of 20% of the total cost of construction as proposed has been invested into the Approved Project prior to submission of the application to the Committee.
program_terms.notes: Regulation 1(2): in force on 1 July 2024. SRO 12 was replaced by SRO 15 of 2024 before commencement; recorded for completeness.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant, at the time of applying for net asset assessment
program_terms.quote: Aged 18 or above at the time of applying for net asset assessment
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect.

program_terms.applies_to: unmarried dependent children (aged under 18) who may come as dependants
program_terms.quote: unmarried dependent children aged under 18 years
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect. 'Under 18' recorded as 18, as in other dependant_child_max_age rows.

program_terms.applies_to: maximum amount of non-residential real estate counted toward the HK$27 million permissible assets
program_terms.quote: Kong, subject to a cap of HK$10 million.
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect.

program_terms.applies_to: maximum counted and ring-fenced as qualifying investment when non-residential real estate worth more than HK$10 million is bought
program_terms.quote: only a maximum of HK$10 million will be counted and ring-fenced as the qualifying investment under the new CIES
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect. Same cap as para 7(g), restated in para 14.

program_terms.currency: percent of the minimum investment threshold
program_terms.applies_to: certificates of deposit denominated in HKD or RMB counted as permissible assets
program_terms.quote: subject to a cap of 10% of the minimum investment threshold
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect.

program_terms.applies_to: minimum remaining term to maturity of certificates of deposit at the time of purchase
program_terms.quote: with a remaining term to maturity of not less than 12 months at the time of purchase
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect.

program_terms.applies_to: maximum visitor stay granted after approval-in-principle to make the committed investment
program_terms.quote: ImmD will grant a visa/entry permit to the applicant for entering Hong Kong as a visitor for not more than 180 days for making the committed investment within the period.
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect.

program_terms.applies_to: permission to stay for the applicant and dependants after formal approval (maximum)
program_terms.quote: Permission to stay will normally be granted to the applicant and his/her dependants (if any) for not more than 24 months on time limitation only
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect.

program_terms.applies_to: each extension of stay after the first 24 months (maximum)
program_terms.quote: may apply for extension of stay for not more than three years, and may subsequently apply for further extension of stay for not more than three years upon the expiry of each period
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect. Number written in words.

program_terms.applies_to: continuous ordinary residence in Hong Kong before applying for permanent residence (applicant and dependants)
program_terms.quote: who upon a period of continuous ordinary residence in Hong Kong of not less than seven years, may apply for becoming Hong Kong permanent residents
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect. Number written in words.

program_terms.applies_to: period of continuously meeting the financial requirements before applying for unconditional stay (if the residence requirement is not met)
program_terms.quote: while continuously satisfying the financial requirements under the new CIES for not less than seven years as verified by InvestHK
program_terms.notes: Legislative Council Brief of 19 December 2023 (Executive Council decision of that day); the brief does not state the date the rule takes effect. Number written in words.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (original CIES launched in 2003)
program_terms.quote: An applicant could make his/her choice of investment at HK$6.5 million in
program_terms.notes: Historical description of the original CIES; the brief says it was launched in 2003.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (original CIES threshold from 2010)
program_terms.quote: In 2010, the investment threshold was increased to HK$10 million. In 2015, the CIES was suspended.
program_terms.notes: Historical description of the original CIES; the brief gives only the years 2010 (increase) and 2015 (suspension).

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the two years before applying
program_terms.location: section 2, table of key numbers (row 'Applications verified as having fulfilled the NAR')
program_terms.quote: applicant has demonstrated that he/she has net assets of not less than HK$30 million in the two years preceding his/her application
program_terms.notes: The release says the scheme launched on 1 March 2024 and that the six-month test replaces the two-year test from 1 March 2025 (section 1(a)(i): 'two years before the enhancement'); valid_to is the day before.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant
program_terms.location: section 2, table of key numbers (row 'Applications verified as having fulfilled the investment requirements')
program_terms.quote: applicant has already made investment of HK$30 million in Hong Kong within the six-month time limit
program_terms.notes: Launch date 1 March 2024 as stated in the release.

program_terms.applies_to: time limit for making the HK$30 million investment
program_terms.location: section 2, table of key numbers (row 'Applications verified as having fulfilled the investment requirements')
program_terms.quote: applicant has already made investment of HK$30 million in Hong Kong within the six-month time limit
program_terms.notes: Number written in words. The Legislative Council Brief (Dec 2023) states the visitor entry for making the investment as not more than 180 days.

ledger.contains: Wayback Machine copy (15 July 2015) of the CBI Unit website page 'Grenada Real Estate': the real-estate option requires 'a minimum investment of USD 350,000' in designated real estate (already recorded as a term) and a list of five government-approved projects with contact details (The Levera Project, Mariposa, Mount Cinnamon Resort and Beach Club, The Point at Petite Calivigny, The Sanctuary at Fiji Beach); no count is printed, so nothing more to record. Note: the existing term t-d11adc5896 attributed to this source (government fee US$50,000 etc.) quotes the separate Fees page archived on 29 June 2015, which is not part of this stored file. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

One-page IMA Grenada 'The CEO's Desk: Processing Report' (2024): text on faster processing (two-track system separating backlog from new applications); a chart of 80 applications processed by processing time (1 to 6 months); a bar chart of applications processed in the first quarter of 2021-2024 (102, 120, 307, 388) with growth rates; annual applications processed 2021-2023 (430, 493, 1,581; already recorded). All numbers extracted except the printed growth rates (18%, 156%, 26%, 'over 300%', 223%), which are comparisons derived from the counts and are not recorded. The period covered by the 80-application chart is not stated (recorded as 2023-2024, basis unspecified). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF Country Report No. 25/39 (February 2025): 2024 Article IV consultation for Grenada, 97 pages. Programme content: Table 1 memo lines CBI inflows and government CBI revenue (percent of GDP) 2019-2029 (also repeated in Table 2); Table 3a (EC$m) and Table 3b (percent of GDP) lines 'Citizenship by Investment Program' (non-tax revenue), 'Bondholder CBI-related payments' and memo 'Government CBI revenue' 2019-2029; text: CBI revenue 10½% of GDP in 2023 (already recorded; repeated in the Executive Director's statement, PDF p. 95), Box 1 programme description (NTF US$235,000; real estate US$270,000 with five-year holding and US$50,000 government contribution, now recorded as terms; Russia/Belarus ban, regional MoA of March 2024 and IMA rebranding already recorded as events) and a scenario assumption (inflows 50% above/below baseline, an assumption, not recorded); policy advice to move all CBI revenue into the NTF; footnotes on bondholders' share of the previous year's CBI revenue, contingency fund transfers and escrow accumulation. All table lines now recorded for every year (two new indicators proposed for the bondholder payments). Not recorded because they are not CBI-only: capital account inflows of 9.5% (2023) and 15% (2024) of GDP 'largely due to the NTF component of CBI', government deposits of 22-23% of GDP, the 2024-25 external accounts text table. Box 1 charts (PDF p. 16) have no printed values. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF first ECF review for Grenada (Dec 2014). Annex II on the new CBI programme: visa-free access table (event exists), fee schedule as of August 2014 (NTF and private-investment rows already recorded; the two 'tranche' rows added as terms), the rule that all budget fees are saved (25-100% of public-sector inflows; added as event), the NTF's monthly EC$2 million transfer for arrears (added as event), and a staff estimate that budget receipts could be 0.2-0.6% of GDP a year (added as a projection range). Fiscal tables have no separate CBI line. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

2025 Budget Statement (March 2025), 46 pages. Programme content: contingency fund (10 percent of NTF receipts) balance of $44.9 million at 31 December 2024 (added; bare '$', currency recorded as unspecified) and the statement that the set-aside was reduced from 40 to 10 percent (no date; see the April 2023 event from the 2026 Budget Statement); unprecedented CBI inflows behind the 2024 primary surplus (no CBI amount); NTF set-aside for Project Polaris from June 2025 (event added); 70% cut in fees for local developers (event already recorded); regional MoA and regional regulator planned for mid-2026 (events exist); automated certification for CBI citizenship (plan). Reports laid with the budget (contingency fund report, MTEFS) are separate documents, not included in this file. The revenue overview has no separate CBI line. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2018' (634 pages; blank divider pages only). Extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' (approved 2017 and forward 2019-2020 added; 2017 provisional and 2018 already in the data); 'CBI Committee' dividend line (five columns; the summary on p. 84 prints '-' where p. 80 prints 0 for 2017, noted); NTF grants (Table 5: 46.8m 2017 estimated outturn; Table 10: 81.1m 2018 budget; text says NTF was 48.8% of external financing while the table says 50.5%, shares not recorded); all lines of the NTF capital-source table (PDF p. 92; 48 project lines plus total; lines add up to the totals; the 2017 approved total here is 32,480,000 against 32,380,000 in the 2017 book). Narrative on NTF-financed housing programmes (over EC$5.5m spent and over EC$2m disbursed in 2017; 1,300 and 117 beneficiaries) repeats table lines or counts beneficiaries of spending, not the programme; not recorded separately. Rest of the budget out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Budget book 'Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure 2021' (635 pages, text throughout). Extracted: item 18001 'CBI Fees' forward 2022-2023 (other columns already in the data); 'CBI Committee' line; NTF grants (Table 6: 85.7m 2020; Table 10: 172.1m 2021 budget); all lines of the NTF capital-source table (PDF p. 90; 97 projects plus total). Column check: project lines sum to 146,072,030 against a printed approved-2020 total of 146,192,030 (120,000 short) and to 85,675,875 against 85,675,873 (rounding); noted on the total rows. Narrative project paragraphs (pp. 42-45): the M-Power 'EC$4.8 million provided for in 2020' differs from the table's 4,000,000 approved (noted on that row); 'Smart Healthcare Facilities - Grenada Phase 2: Total project cost: EC$1 million funded through NTF' (3-year project, no years, not in the NTF table) is recorded with period basis 'unspecified'. Other project paragraphs do not tie amounts to the NTF. Rest of the budget out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Grenada Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2024, S.R.O. 12 of 2024 (4 pages, gazetted 26 June 2024, to commence 1 July 2024): replacement Schedule I with NTF amounts (US$235,000 for main applicant and up to 3 dependants; US$25,000/50,000/75,000 per further dependant by type), approved-project minimum US$350,000, shared unit US$270,000 per share (unit at least US$440,000), government contributions for approved projects and significant investments (US$50,000 plus 25,000/50,000/75,000 per dependant), developer fees (application US$10,000, due diligence US$7,500 for developer and each director, administration US$20,000 a year, start-date extension US$10,000). The four main terms and the price-change event were already recorded; the other 15 amounts are added as program terms. Replaced before commencement by S.R.O. 15 of 2024 (same amounts, unit value corrected to US$540,000). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Legislative Council Brief of 19 Dec 2023 on the New CIES: eligibility (age 18+, eligible nationalities, net assets of HK$30m for two years, no adverse record), minimum investment HK$30m (HK$27m permissible assets incl. non-residential real estate capped at HK$10m and certificates of deposit capped at 10%, plus HK$3m in the CIES Investment Portfolio), portfolio maintenance rules, procedure (InvestHK then ImmD; visitor entry up to 180 days to invest; 24-month then 3-year stays; permanent residence after 7 years), buyer's and new residential stamp duty suspension for applicants, implications, planned launch mid-2024. No application statistics. Investment thresholds, Exco approval and the Budget announcement were already recorded; this pass adds the net-asset requirement as a rule row (caps noted in it). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

InvestHK/FSTB press release of 7 Jan 2025: New CIES enhancements effective 1 Mar 2025 (six-month net-asset test instead of two years, jointly owned assets, holding through a family-owned investment holding vehicle or special purpose entity) and key figures for the first 10 months (enquiries nearly 7,000; applications over 800; 733 passed the net-asset check; 240 passed the investment check; expected investment over HK$24 billion). Also a statement that applications in the first 10 months exceeded those in the same period of the original CIES (no number). The four application figures and the rule-change event were already recorded; this pass adds the enquiries figure (new indicator proposed) and the six-month net-asset rule row. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).
